You cannot return to the Initial Setup Wizard, but all the functions and settings of your Keenetic device are available for manual configuration via the web interface.

search-link.title: Initial Setup Wizard
search-link.description: Initial Setup Wizard is a step-by-step helper in setting up the Internet connection, suitable for most available ISPs.

auth-field.hint: Please type in your full username and password, exactly as supplied by your service provider.

switch-to-extender.title: Switching to Extender Operating Mode
switch-to-extender.description: Follow the instructions to set up your Keenetic device as a Wi-Fi System Extender.
switch-to-extender.software-switch-info: Click Switch to change the operating mode of your device to Extender.
switch-to-extender.hardware-switch-info: Manually switch the device to Extender Mode. Set the selector switch to position B.
switch-to-extender.rebooted-label: The operating mode has been successfully changed to Extender.
switch-to-extender.after-switch-info:
After changing the operating mode, the web interface of your Keenetic device will be available at a new IP address:

  • When connecting to your home network this address is set by the main Keenetic router, and shown on its web interface;
  • When disconnected from your home network, you must use the temporary IP address: 192.168.1.3. Before you can access this temporary IP you must set your computer IP address somewhere between 192.168.1.4 and 192.168.1.254.
  • Please note that the Keenetic device has a separate independent configuration file for each operating mode. The administrator password is empty by default, and if set, it is saved independently for each mode.

waiting-for-reboot.wired-client: Please reconnect to your Keenetic {{model}} device
waiting-for-reboot.detailed-description-wi-fi: After the Keenetic device restarts, wait until both the Status LED {{statusLed}} and the Wi-Fi LED {{wifiLed}} are illuminated and not blinking and then reconnect to the device’s Wi-Fi network ('{{ssid}}') and resume the setup process.
waiting-for-reboot.detailed-description-wired: After the Keenetic device restarts, wait until the {{statusLed}} LED is illuminated and not blinking and then resume the setup process.
waiting-for-reboot.detailed-description-wi-fi-single-led-de: After the Keenetic device restarts, wait until the Status LED is illuminated and not blinking, and then reconnect to the device’s Wi-Fi network ('{{ssid}}') and resume the setup process.
waiting-for-reboot.detailed-description-wired-single-led-de: After the Keenetic device restarts, wait until the Status LED is illuminated and not blinking, and then resume the setup process.

mobile-app-dialog.description: We have detected our mobile app on your mobile device. You can proceed with the setup using the mobile application for added convenience.

double-check-credentials.title: Double-Check Your Credentials
double-check-credentials.description: Your Keenetic device has detected a problem, please check the documentation provided by your ISP, ensuring that your Username and Password for Internet access as entered are correct. If you no longer have this information, you can contact your ISP, and they'll be able to assist you. Please note: Keenetic support doesn't have access to these credentials, and the Username and Password asked for in this section are different to the ones used to log into your Keenetic web interface.

internet-connection-check.title: Internet Connection Check
internet-connection-check.description: Your Keenetic device is now configured for Internet access using the settings you provided. It is trying to connect to the Internet now. This process might take several minutes.

ip-conflict.title: Wait for Your Keenetic Device to Restart
ip-conflict.new-ip-message: Your Keenetic device has detected an IP address conflict with your Internet Service Provider. Your Keenetic device will restart, and the IP address will be updated to {{ip}} to avoid this conflict.
ip-conflict.description: The Initial Setup Wizard will resume automatically. However, if you are connecting by Wi-Fi, you may need to reconnect. After the Keenetic device restarts, wait until both the Status LED {{statusLed}} and the Wi-Fi LED {{wifiLed}} are illuminated and not blinking and then reconnect to the device’s Wi-Fi network and resume the setup process.

review-isp-settings.title: Review Your Settings With Your ISP
review-isp-settings.description: Your Keenetic device was unable to connect to the Internet. Below is the summary of your Internet access settings. Please review the settings to make sure that you have selected and entered the correct options. You can also contact your Internet Service Provider (ISP) to check the configuration information.

access-point.description-os-update-with-date: Click the Apply Settings button below to activate the configuration options you have selected. Your {{model}} will also install the latest KeeneticOS version {{osVersion}}, dated {{osReleaseDate}}. Once the device has restarted, wait until the Wi-Fi LED {{wifiLed}} is solid green. Then unplug the Keenetic Extender, move it to the target location and connect it to the main router using an Ethernet cable.
access-point.description-os-update-without-date: Click the Apply Settings button below to activate the configuration options you have selected. Your {{model}} will also install the latest KeeneticOS version {{osVersion}}. Once the device has restarted, wait until the Wi-Fi LED {{wifiLed}} is solid green. Then unplug the Keenetic Extender, move it to the target location and connect it to the main router using an Ethernet cable.
access-point.description-no-os-update: Click the Apply Settings button below to activate the configuration options you have selected. Once the device has restarted, wait until the Wi-Fi LED {{wifiLed}} is solid green. Then unplug the Keenetic Extender, move it to the target location and connect it to the main router using an Ethernet cable.

extender.description-os-update-with-date:
Click the Apply Settings button below to activate the configuration options you have selected. Your {{model}} will also install the latest KeeneticOS version {{osVersion}}, dated {{osReleaseDate}}. Once the device has restarted, wait until the Wi-Fi LED {{wifiLed}} is solid green. Then unplug the Range Extender and place it within range of your router, about halfway between your router and the Wi-Fi dead zone, to extend your Wi-Fi network.

If you have any questions or need help, please visit {{kbLink}}. We are here to help!

extender.text-part-1:
Tip: Connect a wired-only device to your Keenetic Extender

Besides extending wireless coverage, you can use the Ethernet port on your Keenetic Extender for wired-only devices, such as desktop computers, media players, or game consoles, to connect to your wireless network.
extender.text-part-2: You can also leverage existing Ethernet wiring to connect an extender to your main router. This setup will ensure the best possible performance of your extended network.

bridge.description-os-update-with-date: Click the Apply Settings button below to activate the configuration options you have selected. Your {{model}} will also install the latest KeeneticOS version {{osVersion}}, dated {{osReleaseDate}}. Once the device has restarted, wait until the Wi-Fi LED {{wifiLed}} is solid green. Then unplug the Range Extender and move it within range of your router. Connect your wired device to the Extender using an Ethernet cable.

Connect your wired device to the Extender using an Ethernet cable.

footer.part-1: If you have any questions or need help, please visit {{kbLink}}. We are here to help!
footer.part-2: On your mobile phone, download our app, available on Google Play and the Apple App Store.

auto-update-schedule.title: Schedule Automatic Software Updates
auto-update-schedule.description:
Choose the days and time interval for software updates. You can adjust this schedule at any time through the System Settings.
During the update, your device will restart and stay offline for about one minute. In a Mesh Wi-Fi System, the Controller manages updates for the Extenders.

digital-certificates.title: Installing Trusted Digital Certificates
digital-certificates.description: For safe operation right out of the box, Keenetic deploys individual bank-grade digital encryption certificates to enable protected HTTPS connections to your device. You can continue the initial setup while your Keenetic device obtains a trusted certificate from the Let’s Encrypt certification authority in the background.
digital-certificates.success: From now on, whenever you access the Keenetic web interface, your connection will automatically be protected from eavesdropping and unauthorized access.
digital-certificates.failure: The certificate installation process is initiated. Your Keenetic device will be obtaining a trusted certificate from the Let’s Encrypt certification authority. Please press Next.

description.os-update-available: The Initial Setup Wizard is almost complete. After pressing the Finish button, the device will update the operating system, restart, and apply the new settings.
description.no-os-update: The Initial Setup Wizard is almost complete. After pressing the Finish button, the device will restart and apply the new settings.

progress.update-fail: Please update the device operating system later. The device will now restart with your settings applied.
progress.update-success: The operating system update is successful. Please wait while the device restarts with your settings applied.
progress.reboot-in-progress: Please wait while the device restarts with your settings applied.

product-improvement.title: Join the Product Improvement Programme
product-improvement.description: By sharing anonymous diagnostic and usage data, you help us detect issues more quickly, thereby improving the stability and performance of your device. We collect crash reports and performance metrics, as well as configuration details specific to KeeneticOS. Rest assured, we do not collect your traffic content, browsing history, account names, or passwords. By clicking Join, you consent to the collection and periodic transmission of diagnostic and usage data to Keenetic for product improvement purposes. You can withdraw your consent at any time through the System Settings.
product-improvement.dpn-link-text: See the Device Privacy Notice for more information.

verify-iptv.title: Verify IPTV Service Operation
verify-iptv.description: Connect your operator-branded set-top box (STB) to the port {{port}}, power it up and check if the IPTV service is available and operating correctly.
verify-iptv.description-alternate: Because the IPTV service was not available, alternative settings have been initiated in your Keenetic device. Please remove your set-top box (STB) from the power source for 10 seconds, then plug it in. Make sure your STB is connected to the port {{port}} and check if the IPTV service is available and operating correctly. If the IPTV service is still not operating correctly, contact your ISP for the necessary settings to manually configure the IPTV service on your Keenetic device. Manual configuration can be performed after completing the Initial Setup Wizard.
verify-iptv.description-mvr: Connect your operator-branded set-top box (STB) to the port {{port}}, power it up and check if the IPTV service is available and operating correctly. If the IPTV service is not operating correctly, contact your ISP for the necessary settings to manually configure the IPTV service on your Keenetic device. Manual configuration can be performed after completing the Initial Setup Wizard.
verify-iptv.description-no-free-port: Select a port on the device where you connect the operator-branded set-top box (STB). You can check if the IPTV service is available and operating correctly or skip the IPTV service test for now.

choices.success: IPTV service is available, STB operating correctly
choices.failure: IPTV service is not available or STB operating incorrectly
choices.failure-alternate: IPTV service is still not available or STB operating incorrectly
choices.skip: To skip the IPTV service test

verify-iptv.use-port: Please connect the STB device to the specified port

balanced.title: Balanced performance mode
balanced.description:
• Speeds up to {{maxSpeed}} Mbit/s. Ideal for most homes and small offices.
  • Less interference. More stable in areas with multiple Wi-Fi networks.

max.title: Maximum performance mode
max.description:
• Speeds up to {{maxSpeed}} Mbit/s. Best for VR gaming, large file transfers, and ultra-high-definition streaming.
  • Higher interference. May face more interference in crowded environments.

wifi-settings.title: Wi-Fi Network Settings
wifi-settings.description:
Each Keenetic device has a unique network name and password printed on the factory label of the device. You can keep these or change them.

If you are replacing an older wireless device with a device from Keenetic, you can use the same network name and password, so you do not need to reconfigure connected devices.

your-device-credentials.title: Store Your Keenetic Device Credentials
your-device-credentials.description: Use one of the options below to create a copy of the following important data. This vital system information and configuration options will be useful for future reference.

web-interface.title: Web Interface
web-interface.get-buddy-ip-from-router: Open the user interface of the Main Router to determine the IP address assigned to your Keenetic Buddy.

internet-connection.title: Internet Connection
internet-connection.dedicated-port-message: The Ethernet port {{port}} on your Keenetic device is dedicated to connecting an IPTV STB. There is no access to the Internet from this port.

create-password.title: Secure Your Device
create-password.description: Create an admin password for the router settings. This is not your Wi-Fi password.

buddy.description: Create an admin password for the device settings. This is not your Wi-Fi password.

hint.default: Use uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols.
hint.fair: Fair. Add upper/lower case, numbers, and symbols to make it stronger.

error.blocklist: This password is well-known; please choose a different one.
error.user-name: The password cannot be the same as the username.

initial.description: This Device has a custom configuration. The Wizard will restore the device to factory settings with any custom settings being lost. Please confirm to continue.

reset-in-progress.header: Wait for Your Device to Restart
reset-in-progress.description: The Initial Setup Wizard will resume automatically. However, if you are connecting by Wi-Fi, you may need to reconnect. After the Keenetic device restarts, wait until both the Status LED {{statusLed}} and the Wi-Fi LED {{wifiLed}} are illuminated and not blinking and then reconnect to the device’s Wi-Fi network and resume the setup process.

reset.description: After the restart, the Initial Setup Wizard will launch. Please do not close the page.
reset.question: This Device has a custom configuration. The Wizard will restore the device to factory settings with any custom settings being lost. Please confirm to continue.
reset.warning:
After router restart, please reconnect to this Wi-Fi network:
{{ssid}}

description.via-internal-cellular-modem: Your router will connect to the Internet over mobile data network using the SIM in the built-in slot.
description.via-external-cellular-modem: This device will connect to the Internet using a SIM card in a 3G / 4G LTE / 5G USB modem plugged into the device's USB port.
description.via-dsl: This device will connect to the Internet via a fixed telephone line through a telephone or DSL socket. A telephone cable is contained in your product box.
description.via-sfp-module: This device will connect to the Internet via optical fibre using a market-available SFP module.
description.via-ethernet: Your router will connect to the Internet via Ethernet cable from your provider or Ethernet wall socket.
description.via-ethernet-modem: Your router will connect to the Internet via your provider’s modem/router. Use an Ethernet cable and a spare Ethernet port on the modem.
description.via-wifi: This device will connect to the Internet via a third-party Wi-Fi network.
description.wireless-mws-extender: This device will connect wirelessly to the Keenetic router as part of Keenetic Mesh Wi-Fi System (Keenetic Mesh Extender Mode).
description.wired-mws-extender: This device will connect to the Keenetic router over an Ethernet cable as part of Keenetic Mesh Wi-Fi System (Keenetic Mesh Extender Mode).
description.wireless-range-extender: This device will connect wirelessly to the existing router (regardless of brand) to extend its Wi-Fi network (Range Extender Mode).
description.wired-range-extender: This device will connect to the existing router (regardless of brand) over an Ethernet cable to extend its Wi-Fi network (Range Extender Mode).
description.access-point: This device will connect to the existing router (regardless of brand) via an Ethernet cable to enable wireless access to its network (Access Point Mode).
description.wifi-adapter: This device will operate as an adapter connecting a wired client to a wireless network (Adapter Mode).
description.restore-from-backup: Set up this device by restoring the configuration from a backup file.
description.restore-from-backup-extender: Set up this extender by restoring the configuration from a backup file.

select-country-or-region.description: Select your country/region and time zone. This helps find local providers and sets the right time.

select-scenario-group.description: Pick the setup that suits you.

scenario-group.wifi-adapter: To connect a wired device to an existing Wi-Fi network (Adapter Mode)
scenario-group.restore-backup: Restore settings from a backup file

option.via-dsl: DSL (phone line or DSL wall socket)

welcome.title: Welcome to the Initial Setup Wizard

description.router: Thank you for choosing Keenetic. This quick wizard will help you set up your router and Wi-Fi.
description.extender: Thank you for choosing Keenetic. This quick wizard will help you set up your Wi-Fi extender.
description.access-point: Thank you for choosing Keenetic. This quick wizard will help you set up your Access Point.

agreement-acceptance.eula-dpn: By continuing, you agree to the Keenetic End User Licence Agreement and Device Privacy Notice.
agreement-acceptance.eula: By continuing, you agree to the Keenetic End User Licence Agreement.

dsl-connect-device.title: Connect Your Keenetic Device to the DSL Splitter
dsl-connect-device.description: Use the long telephone cable provided to connect the DSL splitter to your Keenetic device. Ensure that cable connects DSL ports marked DSL on your Keenetic device and the DSL splitter.

dsl-connect-phone.title: Optionally Connect Your Regular Telephone to the DSL Splitter
dsl-connect-phone.description: The PHONE port of your DSL splitter allows you to connect your regular phone using a standard telephone cable. Skip this step if you do not require landline telephony.

dsl-connect-splitter.title: Connect the DSL Splitter to the Telephone Line
dsl-connect-splitter.description: Verify that your DSL service is active. Connect the DSL splitter to the Telephone/DSL wall socket using the short telephone cable provided. Ensure the cable connects to your splitter's LINE port.

dsl-manual-setup.title: Set Up an Internet Connection
dsl-manual-setup.description: When your Internet service starts, your Internet Service Provider typically gives you all the information that you need to connect to the Internet. Enter the following information to connect to the Internet, or contact your service provider for assistance.

dsl-provider.title: Select Your Internet Service Provider
dsl-provider.description: Please select the country and service provider to which you are connecting. In case you have specific settings provided by your service provider, select Other from the list.

fields.dt-login: Fill in data provided by ISP

dsl-setup-iptv.title: Set Up an IPTV Service
dsl-setup-iptv.description: In addition to Internet service, many operators provide an IPTV service with operator-branded set-top box (STB) devices. In order for such service to work, your new Keenetic device must be properly configured. Check with your Internet Service Provider to configure any additional parameters for the IPTV service. This step is optional, and you can configure IPTV service later if you prefer.

connect-modem.title: Connect This Router to Your Modem

description.blue-port: Place the router in an open spot for better Wi-Fi. Keep the modem unplugged for now. Connect the modem to the blue port ({{port}}) on this router using an Ethernet cable.
description.grey-port: Place the router in an open spot for better Wi-Fi. Keep the modem unplugged for now. Connect the modem to the grey port ({{port}}) on this router using an Ethernet cable.
description.red-port: Place the router in an open spot for better Wi-Fi. Keep the modem unplugged for now. Connect the modem to the red port ({{port}}) on this router using an Ethernet cable.

connection-type.title: Select Your Internet Connection Type
connection-type.description: Please specify the type of your Internet connection as follows, for the automatic default Internet access configuration method did not succeed.

type-description.dhcp: Choose this option if your Internet Service Provider did not provide any connection details. Most connections directly from an Ethernet Wall Outlet and Cable modems use this type of connection.
type-description.pppoe: Choose this option if your Internet connection requires Username and Password to get online. Most DSL modems use this type of connection.
type-description.pptp-l2tp: Choose this option if your Internet connection requires Username, Password and Server Address to get online. Some connections directly from an Ethernet Wall Outlet use this type of connection.
type-description.static-ip: Choose this option if your Internet Service Provider provided you with IP Address information that has to be manually entered.

ethernet-provider.title: Select Your Internet Service Provider
ethernet-provider.description: Please select the country and service provider to which you are connecting. In case you have specific settings provided by your service provider, select Other from the list.

import-pppoe-settings.title: Import PPPoE connection settings
import-pppoe-settings.description: Connect the WAN port of the previous router to the indicated port {{port}}, and power it up; your Keenetic device will configure the ISP connection according to the gathered information.

status.connect-to-port: Please connect the WAN port of the previous router to the specified port
status.success:
PPPoE connection settings successfully imported.
Please disconnect the previous router.

ip-config.title: Enter Your IP Address Information
ip-config.description: To setup Static IP address connection type you need to have a complete list of IP information from your Internet Service Provider. If you have a Static IP connection but any of this information is missing, please contact your ISP.

mac-address.title: Choose Which MAC Address to Use
mac-address.description: A MAC address is a unique hardware identification number that lists each device on a network. Some Internet Service Providers use MAC addresses to identify or authenticate your Internet connection. So changing the MAC address of your new Keenetic device to the MAC address of your old router could be a quicker fix than telling your ISP to register the MAC of your new Keenetic device.

select-wan-port.title: Choose the Internet Port
select-wan-port.title-modem: Choose the Port for Modem Connection
select-wan-port.description:
Pick the Ethernet port that will connect to your provider's modem or Ethernet cable.
Do not plug the cable in yet — you will do this shortly.
select-wan-port.description-default-blue-fast-orange: Pick the Ethernet port that will connect to your provider's modem or Ethernet cable. If your service is faster than {{defaultPortMaxSpeed}}, choose the orange {{fastPortMaxSpeed}} port ({{fastPortLabel}}). In this case, the blue port {{defaultPortLabel}} becomes a home network port. Do not plug the cable in yet — you will do this shortly.
select-wan-port.description-2_5G-Sfp: Pick the port that will connect to your provider's optical or Ethernet cable. If your service is faster than 1 Gbit/s, or if you want to use an SFP transceiver for a fibre connection, choose the orange port {{orangePort}}. In this case, the blue port {{bluePort}} becomes a home network port. Do not plug the cable in yet — you will do this shortly.
select-wan-port.description-2_5G-Sfp-modem: Pick the Ethernet port that will connect to your provider's modem. If the Ethernet port on your modem is faster than 1 Gbit/s, choose the orange 2.5 Gbit/s port {{orangePort}}. In this case, the blue port {{bluePort}} becomes a home network port. Do not plug the cable in yet — you will do this shortly.
select-wan-port.switch-user-port-warning: Please select any grey Ethernet port to connect your computer to the Keenetic device. The current port will be configured for Internet connection.

pppoe.title: Enter Your Credentials
pppoe.description: To setup PPPoE Internet connection type you need to know your Username and Password from your Internet Service Provider (ISP). If you do not have this information, please contact your ISP.

pptp-l2tp.title: Enter Your Credentials
pptp-l2tp.description: To setup the PPTP or L2TP Internet connection type, you need to know your Username, Password, and Authentication Server Address from your Internet Service Provider (ISP). If you do not have this information, please contact your ISP.

unplug-modem.title: Unplug Your Modem
unplug-modem.desc_begin: Unplug your DSL, fibre, cable or satellite modem from the mains. If it has a backup battery, remove it. If other wireless equipment is connected to the modem, unplug that too. Keep it unplugged until further instructions.
unplug-modem.desc_end: If you have no modem and your Internet connection is through a direct Ethernet cable and/or your Internet connection involves VLAN settings, choose I have no modem.

vlan-setup.title: Manual Internet Setup
vlan-setup.description: Automatic setup did not detect your connection. Some providers use VLAN IDs for Internet and IPTV/set-top boxes (STBs). If your provider has provided VLAN details, enter them below. Otherwise, select Next to continue.

vlan-information.title: Enter VLAN Information
vlan-information.description: Check with your Internet Service Provider if it is necessary to configure a VLAN number for the Internet in your Keenetic device. If not, proceed without VLAN number.

wan-via-sfp.title: Plug an SFP Transceiver Into Your Keenetic Device
wan-via-sfp.description: Connect the fibre optic cable from your ISP to the SFP transceiver. Insert the SFP transceiver into an SFP slot on your Keenetic device. For the list of known compatible SFP transceivers, please visit {{supportSite}}. Consult your Internet Service Provider to make sure that your line is ready and that the service is available.

wan-via-modem.title: Power On Your Modem
wan-via-modem.description: Reconnect any backup battery first, then plug the modem into the mains. Wait about two minutes for it to restart and for the lights to become steady.

wan-via-wall-outlet.title: Connect to Your Provider’s Ethernet
wan-via-wall-outlet.title-sfp-port-4: Connect the Cable from Your ISP

description.blue-port:
• If there’s a loose Ethernet cable from your provider, plug it into the blue port ({{port}}) on this router.
  • If you have a wall socket installed by your provider, connect it to the blue port ({{port}}) with an Ethernet cable.
  • If the line isn’t active, contact your provider.

description.red-port:

  • If you have a wall socket installed by your provider, connect it to the red port ({{port}}) with an Ethernet cable.

description.sfp-port-4: Connect the Ethernet cable from your ISP to the red port marked 4. Or connect the fibre optic cable from your ISP to the SFP transceiver and insert it into the SFP slot on your Keenetic device. Consult with your provider to make sure that your line is ready and that the service is available.

description.generic: Use this device as a Wi-Fi extender. Follow these steps. 1. Choose mode — Set the Operating Mode Switch on the side of this device to position B to switch to the Extender mode. 2. Connect by cable — After the device restarts and the Status LED {{statusLed}} and Wi-Fi LED {{wifiLed}} are solid (not flashing), connect it to your Main Router with the supplied Ethernet cable. Make sure both are powered. The Internet LED {{internetLed}} on the extender should be solid. 3. Join the Main Router’s network — Reconnect your phone/computer to the Main Router via Wi-Fi or Ethernet. 4. Add the extender — Open Wi-Fi System on the Main Router, find this device, and select Acquire. 5. Place the extender — Extender mode supports wired or wireless backhaul links. After setup, you can unplug the cable and place the extender where you need better coverage.

select-extra-segments.title: Create Additional Wi-Fi Networks
select-extra-segments.description: Clients on separate networks will be isolated from each other. Each network will have a unique name (SSID) and password. You may customize these settings now if you wish.

guest.label: Guests Network
guest.description: Allow visitors to access the Internet without letting them into your primary network.

iot.label: IoT Network
iot.description: A network for your smart devices.

kids.label: Kids Network
kids.description: A network for your children that is active from 10 to 19 hours and filters unsafe content.

teens.label: Teens Network
teens.description: A network for your older children that is active from 8 to 21 hours.

error.not-unique: This name is already in use

encryption.label: Network protection
encryption.hint:
Select the WPA2-PSK protocol for broad compatibility with legacy client devices while assuring optimal connection security.

Using WPA2-PSK + WPA3-PSK allows for enhanced security with modern clients.

For maximum protection of a modern-only clients' network, choose WPA3-PSK instead.

wifi-bands.label: Wi-Fi bands
wifi-bands.hint:
Your dual-band Keenetic device uses two carrier frequencies (bands) for Wi-Fi: 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz.

The 2.4 GHz band has longer reach, but lower speed. The 5 GHz band offers faster speeds, but shorter reach.

For an IoT network it is recommended to enable only the 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi for greater compatibility. For all other Wi-Fi networks it is recommended to use both bands.

is-active-on-schedule.label: Active on a schedule
is-active-on-schedule.hint:
Adjust these time intervals according to your family's daily routine.

Important: This feature helps to develop healthy habits, but is only an additional precautionary measure and does not replace parental supervision.

For the latest information, please refer to the recommendations of specialist institutions in your area.

lte-double-check-sim.title: Check Your SIM Card
lte-double-check-sim.description: Unable to connect to the mobile network. Make sure the settings match your provider’s advice and the SIM is active and undamaged. If possible, test the SIM in another device in the same location.

lte-external-antenna.title: Optional External Antenna
lte-external-antenna.description: For a stronger mobile signal, you can add a third-party external high-gain antenna (not included). It screws onto the same connectors as the supplied antennas.

lte-install-antennas.title: Attach the Mobile Antennas
lte-install-antennas.description: Screw on the supplied antennas as shown. Hand-tighten only, and position them vertically.

lte-network-connection.title: Connecting to the Mobile Network
lte-network-connection.description: Your router is searching for your mobile network. This can take a few minutes.

lte-pin-code.title: Enter the SIM PIN Code
lte-pin-code.description: Enter the PIN code for this SIM card. You have three tries, after which it locks and needs a PUK code from your mobile provider.

sim-pin.last-pin-attempt-confirm: This is your last attempt to enter a valid PIN. The SIM card will be locked immediately when you enter an incorrect PIN code this time.
sim-pin.pin-attempts-left: {{num}} attempts left to enter the PIN code.

lte-review-params.title: Review Settings and Try Again
lte-review-params.description: Update these if your mobile provider gave different details, then try again.

lte-signal-level.title: You Are Online

signal-level-indicator.no-mobile-operator: Mobile connection established, signal strength is {{signalLevelLabel}}.

legend.internet-led: The Internet LED {{internetLed}} shows the network type.
legend.mobile-network-led: The Mobile Network LED {{baseStationLed}} indicates signal strength.

lte-signal-level.no-mobile-operator-description: Mobile connection established, signal strength is {{signalLevelLabel}}.
lte-signal-level.hint: For a stronger signal, try moving the router closer to a window or placing it higher up.
lte-signal-level.color-legend: The Internet LED {{internetLed}} shows the network type. The Mobile Network LED {{baseStationLed}} colour shows the signal strength.

lte-sim-card.title: Insert Your SIM Card
lte-sim-card.description: Insert a SIM card with the gold contacts facing down into the SIM slot on the back of your Keenetic device until you hear a click. To obtain an activated SIM card, contact your mobile broadband service provider.
lte-sim-card.description-2-sim-slots: Insert a SIM card with the gold contacts facing down into the SIM 1 slot on the side of your Keenetic device until you hear a click. To obtain an activated SIM card, contact your mobile broadband service provider.

lte-verify-operator.title: Check with Your Mobile Provider
lte-verify-operator.description:
Unable to connect to the mobile network. Please check:
  • The SIM is active and supports data.
  • Mobile data is enabled on your account.
  • You’re in coverage, or data roaming is on (if needed).
  • You have enough credit/data.
  • The APN settings for this SIM are correct (APN/username/password).

upload-configuration.select-on-drag-file: Drag the backup file here, or browse
